The secret sauce is a modular system that allows players to create and explore a unique ecosystem each time they play. Adapt to the Changing Environment: Grow thriving populations in an ecosystem where food is scarce and predators lurk. Evolve traits like Tusked for foraging, Fast for escaping danger, or Clawed for hunting. Create a Unique Ecosystem Each Time You Play: The core game of Nature is an accessible gateway into a world of dynamic ecosystems. Add the Jurassic module for a more aggressive game with colossal dinosaurs, or the Arctic Tundra module to experience life on the edge of the habitable world. There are currently 5 modules and 2 mini-modules that can be combined to create 96 different ecosystems. After the GenCon 2026 release of Climate module and 2 new mini-modules, there will be over 700 combinations to explore! Preparation Phase 1.2 2. Adapting Phase 1.3 3. Feeding Phase 1.4 4. Scoring Overview Nature is a card-driven tableau-builder played over four rounds. You score points by feeding your species and keeping them alive. Each round has four phases. 1. Preparation Phase Add plant food to the watering hole based on the player count and the top card of the deck. Gain a new species starting at size 1 and population 1. Add any population or size lost during the previous round to this new species. Draw 5 cards. There is no hand limit. 2. Adapting Phase Players take one turn to modify their species. You can perform these actions as many times as you want: Increase Population: Discard a card to add 1 population to a species. Increase Size: Discard a card to increase a species' size by 1 (maximum size is 4). Play a Trait: Play a card face-down near a species to grant it an ability (maximum 3 traits per species, including Hunter). Free Actions: Add a Hunter card from the supply to turn a species into a carnivore, remove existing traits, or save cards for later. 3. Feeding Phase Players take turns feeding one hungry species at a time until all population is fed or dead Forage: Foragers eat plants from the watering hole equal to their size. Hunt: Hunters eat meat from the supply equal to their prey's size. A hunter's hunt value must be equal to or greater than the prey's defense value. The hunted species loses 1 population. Starve: If a species cannot forage or hunt, it must starve and lose 1 population. Free Action: Discard cards from your hand before a feeding action to add their food value in plants to the watering hole. 4. Scoring At the end of each round, move all eaten food behind your screen. After four rounds, you score 1 point for every food token eaten and 2 bonus points for each surviving species. The player with the most points wins. If there's a tie, the player with the most cards played as Traits wins. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] This game has nothing to do with the game called Evolution that was released by Rightgames in 2010. Their new name and their tagline is trying to get you to make that connection.

[Rating: 1/10] This is just a rebranded Evolution.  But the designer is just Dominic and should credit the original creators: Dmitry Knorre, Sergey Machin.  This was there system and it looks like Northstar Games just took their IP and rebranded it without them.

[Rating: 1/10] Variety of trait cards is too limited to make the game interesting. There are modules to improve this but I would expect the basic game to have a lot more meat to it. My preference goes to Evolution New World.

[Rating: 2/10] They took out abilities and made the base game worse so that they can sell you the expansions. The base game is boring and doesn't really work, they knew this because there's been so many iterations of Evolution. Not fun and also anti-consumer.

[Rating: 2/10] This is a review of the Nature game by itself, without any "Module".  The game reuse some trait cards (of the very few it has) from the "Evolution: Climate" game, which is both disappointing and feels a bit like a rip off.  It is pretty much the same concept, without the changing climate, and stripped down to the bare minimum.   I pre-ordered the game with 5 modules, which I haven't played yet, but the base game by itself is not worth much, and it seems overpriced considered it is pretty much a stripped down version of the older Climate game.

[Rating: 2/10] Spel is veel te simplistisch in zijn natuur. Slechts 4 rondes en je hebt niet veel keuzemogelijkheden. Er zitten hier weinig tactieken achter.  Je hebt op zich maar 3 keuzes: Increase population, increase size of speel de kaart voor een trait.  Echt veel keuzes zijn dit niet voor een competitief spel.

[Rating: 3/10] The game needs a better UI/UX. The traits for one species are unstuckable - some important info on the top of the card, some on the bottom. Due to this, it's tough to count the defence amount or features of other players' species.   It's positioned as a redesign of evolution. But looks like a poor result of trying to do so.  + I don't get this whole redesign idea with the new project, excluding the creator of Evolution. Like you're promoting your project using the Evolution game but without any benefits to its creator.

[Rating: 3/10] as boring as you can get with a nature team. Feeding pools, transform into hunters, grow in size and population, uninspired tactics and mechanics, it doesn't appeal to me at all.

[Rating: 3/10] I knew I was over this game the moment an event got drawn that said "you can no longer do the fundamental action in the game and also kill 3 of your population :)". Never again...

[Rating: 3/10] "What an interesting design decision" - Nizar, after we flipped the event card that said foraging is now impossible

[Rating: 3/10] I supported the kickstarter und have all expansions. I am also a big fan of evolution and evolution climate. The star rating is for the base game only.   We played the base game twice in our group. The presentation is fantastic. The gameplay it is quite boring in myopinion. There are very few traits and none are particularly interesting. Also there is no good way of getting around defences.  In my opinion the expansions are absolutely necessary. With those I can recommend this game wholeheartedly. They add a lot of dept and were very well percieved by myself and my group. Without the expansion

[Rating: 3/10] Really shallow and no interesting decisions. Too much take-that Maybe better with modules...
